rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis lists exactly the same interventions as the hidden target: comparison of thin films and nanoribbon arrays with 1 and 2 µm spacing, cyclic longitudinal tensile strain of 0–1% and 0–2% on films, and annealing of 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons at 700 K in Ar + 2% N2, all fabricated by five-source magnetron co-sputtering after e-beam lithography.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis reproduces the paper's conditions verbatim, including structural characterization by TEM/SAED and AFM, SQUID measurements from 2–300 K under 1 kOe in ZFC/FC modes with parallel/perpendicular fields, hysteresis loops at 5 and 300 K, magnetocaloric isotherms from 5–200 K up to 50 kOe with Maxwell-relation entropy change, and elastic strain limited to 2%.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis states the same mechanisms as the target: annealing-induced short-range reordering and strain relaxation reduce domain-pinning barriers and increase ferromagnetic volume fraction; longitudinal strain acts via magnetoelastic coupling to stabilize magnetic order above 100 K while preserving in-plane isotropy; increased ribbon spacing suppresses inter-ribbon coupling; and edge-related spin frustration reduces nanoribbon magnetization relative to films.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The predicted outcomes match the target exactly: 700 K annealing enhances magnetization and maximum −ΔSM of 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons without crystallization; elastic strain strengthens magnetic response above 100 K without shifting the blocking peak or breaking in-plane isotropy; and 2 µm spacing eliminates coupling-related in-plane anisotropy.
